query: The Daughters' Shortcut Pell's daughters say there's a shortcut: learn what the draught takes out of a brewer by tasting a little of it first. "Father hates it," says one. "It works," says the other. "You'll be ill for a day." Try it on yourself It takes the strength out of your knees and then, slowly, gives it back. You spend a day in bed. When you get up, you know exactly where the draught will pull from. Do it Pell's way You decline. The daughters shrug. Pell, who was listening, corrects a label more firmly than it needed.
